title.en: You Don't Know How You Feel Until You Write It Down
title.de: Du weißt nicht, wie du fühlst, bis du es aufschreibst

excerpt.en: Writing isn't how I record what I think — it's how I find out. On the gap between having a feeling and actually knowing it.
excerpt.de: Schreiben ist nicht, wie ich festhalte, was ich denke — es ist, wie ich es herausfinde. Über die Lücke zwischen einem Gefühl und dem wirklichen Wissen darum.

body.en:
I often don't know what I think — or how I feel — until I've written it down. The feeling exists, but it's a fog. Writing is the thing that condenses it into something I can actually look at.

This surprises people who assume writing is just transcription: you have the finished thought, you type it out. For me it's the opposite. The thought gets *finished by* the typing.

## Why the page knows more than my head

- It forces one word after another — no vague simultaneous blur.
- It makes contradictions visible; you can't hide them in a sentence.
- It slows me to the speed of actually noticing.

## The two modes

- **Capture:** get it out of my head before it evaporates (see the note-taking post).
- **Discovery:** write *toward* a feeling I can't yet name, until the sentence surprises me.

## Notes to self

- A real example: a decision I only understood after journaling it.
- Careful not to romanticize — sometimes writing muddies too. When does it help vs. spiral?
